articles.title: Spa da Floresta levou experiência sensorial ao Inova Amazônia Summit 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Além da massoterapia, o espaço contou com a medicina da Floresta aplicada por indígenas do povo Huni Kui
articles.summary: Além da massoterapia, o espaço contou com a medicina da Floresta aplicada por indígenas do povo Huni Kui
articles.body:
Indígena realiza pintura corporal em visitante. — Foto: Pedro Nascimento

O Inova Amazônia Summit 2026, evento realizado pelo Sebrae , é o principal encontro de bioeconomia, inovação e empreendedorismo da Amazônia Legal. Durante três dias, empreendedores, startups, pesquisadores, investidores, lideranças empresariais, representantes do setor público e especialistas do Brasil e do mundo se conectaram para transformar o potencial da biodiversidade amazônica em negócios sustentáveis, soluções inovadoras e desenvolvimento econômico com impacto positivo para a floresta e para as pessoas.

Como parte da programação, o Spa da Floresta foi projetado para oferecer ao público do Inova Amazônia Summit 2026, relizado em Rio Branco, capital do Acre, uma experiência sensorial com base na biodiversidade amazônica, com o uso de aromas, óleos essenciais locais, sons da mata e rituais que conectam saberes ancestrais.

No espaço montado na Casa do Seringueiro, as atividades de massoterapia, além da medicina da floresta aplicada por indígenas convidados, foram disponibilizadas aos visitantes durante os três dias do evento, iniciado na quinta-feira, 17, e que seguiu até o último sábado, 19, no campus da Universidade Federal do Acre (Ufac).

Organizadora do espaço Spa da Floresta fala sobre atendimentos no espaço de experiência sensorial. — Foto: Pedro Nascimento

“Nós estamos trazendo a massoterapia, que são as massagens, massagem relaxante, as ventosas, a massagem dos pés. E também, nós temos os indígenas que estão oferecendo a medicina da floresta, como rapé, sananga, a pintura, que é a pintura com o urucum e a pintura com o genipapo. Essas são as medicinas da floresta” , disse a empresária e organizadora do Spa da Floresta, Rosiany de Sá.

A massoterapeuta Francineide da Silva Damasceno, explica que o espaço é importante para que os visitantes possam ter um momento para relaxar em meio a extensa agenda de três dias do evento.

Francineide realiza ventosaterapia em participante do evento. — Foto: Pedro Nascimento

“Nesse momento de cansaço, de estresse, a ventosa tem como objetivo ajudar no relaxamento, diminuir o estresse, a pressão e a ansiedade. Então ela tem esses objetivos tanto a ventosa quanto a massagem terapêutica, e tem também a reflexoterapia que é liberar pontos pelos pés, pelas mãos, pescoços e diafragma” , explicou a massoterapeuta.

Estudante aproveita momento relaxante em meio à programação extensa do Inova Amazônia Summit. — Foto: Pedro Nascimento

A estudante Julia Lima aproveitou uma pausa entre uma palestra e outra para visitar o espaço de massagens e garantir um momento para relaxar. “Foi maravilhoso, eu gostei muito. Até porque a gente está aí esses três dias na correria de um lado para o outro e dá essa pausazinha também é importante” , disse Julia.

articles.standfirst: Evento reuniu estudantes, autoridades e instituições no Itaperuna Tênis Clube.
articles.summary: Evento reuniu estudantes, autoridades e instituições no Itaperuna Tênis Clube.
articles.body:
O Dia da Árvore foi celebrado nesta segunda-feira (21) com uma ação de educação e preservação ambiental em Itaperuna , no Noroeste Fluminense. Realizado pela Prefeitura, o evento no Itaperuna Tênis Clube (ITC) reuniu estudantes, autoridades, representantes de instituições e moradores. A iniciativa distribuiu cerca de cinco mil mudas gratuitamente e também ofereceu serviços à população.

A ação incentivou o plantio de árvores em quintais, propriedades rurais e outros espaços do município. Segundo os organizadores, ao longo das seis edições do evento, cerca de 30 mil mudas já foram distribuídas.

A iniciativa também promoveu o plantio de mudas em outros pontos de Itaperuna. A ação reúne diferentes instituições e parceiros com o objetivo de incentivar o plantio de árvores e ampliar a conscientização sobre a importância da preservação ambiental.

Sexta ediçãDia da Árvore distribui 5 mil mudas de árvore em Itaperuna — Foto: Diego Varsi

Além das atividades voltadas ao meio ambiente, a programação contou com uma equipe de vacinação e atendimento para retirada de documentos.

articles.title: Discord remove aplicativos usados para contornar suspensão de vídeos ao vivo no Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Depois de reportagem da GloboNews, empresa reconheceu que serviços de terceiros eram utilizados dentro da plataforma para contornar a restrição determinada pela ANPD e afirmou que retirou os aplicativos do ar.
articles.summary: Depois de reportagem da GloboNews, empresa reconheceu que serviços de terceiros eram utilizados dentro da plataforma para contornar a restrição determinada pela ANPD.
articles.body:
O Discord afirmou nesta segunda-feira (21) que removeu da plataforma aplicativos de terceiros que estavam sendo utilizados para contornar a suspensão dos recursos de vídeo no Brasil, determinada pela Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD).

A declaração foi dada à GloboNews após a reportagem identificar que pelo menos dois serviços externos continuavam disponíveis dentro de funções nativas do Discord e permitiam a transmissão e o compartilhamento de vídeo em tempo real durante chamadas coletivas.

A plataforma confirma que os aplicativos identificados pela reportagem estavam sendo utilizados dentro do Discord. Segundo a empresa, porém, isso ocorria sem sua autorização e em desacordo com os termos de uso.

A plataforma disse ainda que agiu imediatamente para remover os aplicativos e que a medida faz parte dos procedimentos adotados para cumprir leis e exigências regulatórias.

“Após investigarmos o uso de aplicativos de terceiros para contornar a suspensão dos recursos de vídeo no Brasil, sem o conhecimento ou a aprovação do Discord, agimos imediatamente para remover esses aplicativos da plataforma, em conformidade com nossos termos”, afirmou a empresa.

O Discord também afirmou que continua em diálogo com a ANPD para tentar restabelecer os recursos de vídeo para usuários brasileiros. (veja a nota abaixo)

A ANPD informou que, após receber a denúncia da GloboNews , solicitou ao Discord esclarecimentos sobre o caso. Segundo a agência, o descumprimento de medidas preventivas pode levar a novas medidas, entre elas a aplicação de multa diária.

A GloboNews identificou pelo menos dois serviços externos disponíveis dentro do Discord que permitiam o compartilhamento e a transmissão de vídeo em tempo real durante chamadas coletivas.

Os serviços não eram desenvolvidos pelo Discord, mas podiam ser utilizados dentro da própria plataforma. Nos testes realizados pela reportagem, os recursos funcionavam para usuários no Brasil, mesmo após a determinação da ANPD.

A empresa não informou quando os aplicativos foram retirados nem quais mecanismos técnicos adotou para impedir que serviços semelhantes sejam usados para contornar a suspensão.

Segundo os investigadores, a adolescente morreu durante uma transmissão ao vivo. A investigação aponta que ela teria sido induzida ao suicídio por pessoas que mantinham contato com ela em grupos fechados da internet.

A investigação deu origem à Operação Lívia, conduzida pela Polícia Civil e pelo Ministério da Justiça.

“Após investigarmos o uso de aplicativos de terceiros para contornar a suspensão dos recursos de vídeo no Brasil, sem o conhecimento ou a aprovação do Discord, agimos imediatamente para remover esses aplicativos da plataforma, em conformidade com nossos termos. Como parte de nossos processos de aplicação das regras, adotamos medidas sempre que necessário para cumprir as leis aplicáveis ou exigências regulatórias. Seguimos em diálogo ativo com a ANPD em busca de uma solução que permita restabelecer os recursos de vídeo para os usuários do Discord no Brasil.”

"A Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD) informa que, a partir da denúncia recebida, já solicitou ao Discord esclarecimentos sobre o conteúdo apresentado pela GloboNews. O descumprimento de medidas preventivas pode gerar a imposição de novas medidas, como, por exemplo, a aplicação de multa diária.

A Superintendência de Fiscalização (SFI-ANPD) decidiu manter a interrupção temporária das transmissões ao vivo do Discord ao indeferir o pedido de efeito suspensivo da medida preventiva apresentado no recurso da plataforma, por entender que a retomada das lives e do compartilhamento de vídeos ao vivo, sem a adoção de medidas que tornem essa funcionalidade mais segura para crianças e adolescentes, poderia gerar risco de repetição das condutas investigadas e de novos danos antes mesmo da conclusão do processo de fiscalização, que segue em curso desde o dia 07/08.

A área técnica reforça que a suspensão das transmissões ao vivo tem caráter temporário e sua reversão continua condicionada à demonstração, pelo Discord, da implementação de salvaguardas capazes de mitigar os riscos identificados, sem impedir a continuidade das demais funcionalidades da plataforma. A empresa e a SFI seguem em diálogo sobre as medidas a serem implementadas para garantir a proteção de crianças e adolescentes.

O mérito dos demais itens do recurso do Discord foi analisado pela SFI e seguiu, na última quinta-feira (17), para o Conselho Diretor da ANPD, instância responsável por decidir o recurso em caráter final na via administrativa."

articles.title: Montanha-russa nos EUA acumula casos de lesões cerebrais, diz TV | G1
articles.standfirst: Atração X2, no parque de diversões Six Flags, na Califórnia, está ligada a dezenas de incidentes, segundo investigação da CNN Internacional.
articles.summary: Atração X2, no parque de diversões Six Flags, na Califórnia, está ligada a dezenas de incidentes, segundo investigação da CNN Internacional.
articles.body:
Fachada do parque Six Flag Magic Mountain, na Califórnia — Foto: By Jeremy Thompson from United States of America - Six Flags Magic Mountain, CC BY 2.0

Uma montanha-russa extrema em um parque de diversões nos Estados Unidos acumula diversos casos de lesões cerebrais graves e que alguns deles resultaram até em mortes, segundo uma investigação da TV CNN Internacional.

Os casos mais recentes foram de duas mulheres que tiveram que ser submetidas a cirurgias de emergência com hemorragia cerebral após andarem na atração X2, do parque Six Flags, na Califórnia. Esses incidentes ocorreram separadamente em julho e se assemelham com o caso de Júlia, que perdeu os movimentos após andar em uma atração no Hopi Hari.

Segundo a CNN Internacional, o X2 está ligado a casos de lesões graves, hospitalizações e até mortes de pessoas que adoeceram logo após deixar a montanha-russa ao longo de um período de quase duas décadas.

"Entre as vítimas estão pessoas que sofreram deficiências que mudaram suas vidas, entraram em coma e duas que morreram em decorrência dos ferimentos", afirmou a reportagem.

Os relatos à TV norte-americana foram similares à história contada por João Pedro Bossoni, marido de Júlia, ao Fantástico: o turista apresenta sintomas extremos, como tontura, desmaios ou até convulsões por ter batido a cabeça durante uma viagem de montanha-russa , e depois tem que ser encaminhado com urgência para o hospital.

O Six Flags foi inaugurado em 1971 e montanha-russa X2, em 2001. Apesar dos diversos casos graves e das denúncias de segurança ao longo dos anos, a atração continua aberta.

Especialistas ouvidos pela CNN Internacional afirmaram que o risco de lesões cerebrais traumáticas associadas a montanhas-russas é considerado muito baixo, porém não há razão para um brinquedo ser projetado sem os devidos requisitos para evitar tais incidentes.

articles.title: Governo Trump rebate críticas de jornalistas e diz que acesso à Casa Branca é 'privilégio, não direito' | G1
articles.standfirst: Governo Trump reiterou a proibição da CNN, MS NOW e Politico da cobertura do executivo do país após outras televisões anunciarem saída
articles.summary: Governo Trump reiterou a proibição da CNN, MS NOW e Politico da cobertura do executivo do país após outras televisões anunciarem saída
articles.body:
A Casa Branca voltou a defender a proibição a jornalistas de veículos tidos como críticos à gestão de Donald Trump nas dependências presidenciais. Em comunicado divulgado nesta segunda-feira (21), o governo afirmou que o acesso de veículos de imprensa às dependências da sede do Executivo americano é um “privilégio”, e não um direito .

O governo afirmou que os meios de comunicação publicaram informações que classificou como falsas e disse que a constituição do país garante o direito de publicação, mas não o acesso às dependências do palácio.

A nota é mais um capítulo do embate iniciado entre Trump e os jornais de oposição. Na última sexta-feira (18), o republicano anunciou que barraria os repórteres da CNN, MS Now e do site Politico e a medida começou a ser aplicada no sábado (19). Jornalistas dos três veículos tiveram as credenciais recolhidas ou desativadas .

Nesta segunda, os três veículos anunciaram que vão processar o governo federal. Em comunicado conjunto, afirmaram que a Casa Branca retirou as credenciais dos jornalistas sem aviso prévio e em reação às suas coberturas factuais.

Outras quatro redes de TV americanas anunciaram que vão suspender a cobertura conjunta que fazem do governo dos EUA , em solidaridade.

Casa Branca proíbe entrada de repórteres. — Foto: JN

A Casa Branca, por sua vez, acusou os veículos de produzir “reportagens falsas” e afirmou que Trump não é obrigado a permitir a presença de veículos que, segundo o governo, mantêm uma cobertura hostil à administração.

O comunicado cita um levantamento do Media Research Center, segundo o qual 92% da cobertura dos principais veículos de imprensa sobre os primeiros 100 dias do segundo mandato de Trump foi negativa.

O governo afirmou que a imprensa estaria atuando como uma “operação política com câmeras”. Segundo a nota, Trump estaria apenas aplicando uma regra segundo a qual o acesso presidencial não é garantido a todos os veículos.

articles.title: Eleições na Rússia: 49 veteranos de guerra são eleitos para a Duma | G1
articles.standfirst: Veteranos passam a ocupar cerca de 11% das cadeiras da Duma, câmara baixa do Parlamento russo, em uma eleição marcada por críticas à falta de oposição à guerra. Kremlin celebrou resultado e falou em 'coesão' em torno do presidente, já o bloco europeu chamou eleição de 'erosão da democracia'.
articles.summary: Nas eleições na Rússia, veteranos de guerra da Ucrânia conquistaram 11% das cadeiras da Duma com apoio de Vladimir Putin, sob críticas da União Europeia.
articles.body:
A nova composição do Parlamento da Rússia terá 49 deputados que participaram da guerra contra a Ucrânia , segundo o Rússia Unida, partido governista de Vladimir Putin , que divulgou as informações nesta segunda-feira (21). O número representa a presença de ex-combatentes em uma instituição que, após a eleição deste mês, ficou ainda mais alinhada ao Kremlin.

Os 49 veteranos foram eleitos pelo partido governista, de acordo com Vladimir Yakushev, secretário-geral do Rússia Unida. Inicialmente, ele havia informado que 86 participantes da chamada “operação militar especial” seriam eleitos, mas posteriormente corrigiu o número para 49.

A eleição foi a primeira para a Duma, a Câmara Baixa do Parlamento russo, desde a invasão em larga escala da Ucrânia, em 2022. O resultado também ampliou a presença do Rússia Unida no Legislativo: o partido ficou com 355 das 450 cadeiras , segundo resultados preliminares, o maior número de assentos já obtido pela legenda.

Com isso, os veteranos passam a ocupar cerca de 11% das cadeiras da Duma . A presença deles ocorre em um Parlamento no qual os principais partidos que conquistaram assentos também apoiam a campanha militar russa na Ucrânia .

O Partido Comunista ficou com 40 cadeiras, o LDPR, de perfil ultranacionalista, com 25, e o Novos Povos, com 20. A composição deixa a oposição à guerra praticamente fora do Parlamento federal.

👉 A supermaioria obtida desta vez é superior ao recorde anterior, registrado em 2016, quando o Rússia Unida conseguiu 343 cadeiras no Duma.

Presidente da Rússia, Vladimir Putin, durante discurso em 18 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Sputnik/Alexander Kazakov/Pool via REUTERS

O pleito foi realizado em meio a forte controle político e críticas de governos ocidentais. O partido Yabloko, única legenda registrada que se opunha à guerra, foi impedido pela Suprema Corte russa de disputar a eleição nacional.

A União Europeia classificou a votação como um retrocesso para a democracia russa. A votação também ocorreu em áreas da Ucrânia ocupadas pela Rússia, onde Moscou realizou eleições apesar de a anexação desses territórios não ser reconhecida internacionalmente.

Veteranos ganham espaço na política russa

A eleição dos 49 veteranos ocorre enquanto o governo russo tenta incorporar à vida política do país pessoas que participaram diretamente da guerra contra a Ucrânia .

Segundo dados divulgados pela comissão eleitoral, 186 participantes ou veteranos da guerra haviam se registrado como candidatos à Duma . Desse grupo, 110 estavam nas listas partidárias e 76 disputavam vagas em distritos de candidatura única.

A presença dos ex-combatentes no Parlamento acontece enquanto a guerra continua. Nas últimas semanas, a Rússia intensificou os ataques contra cidades ucranianas, enquanto a Ucrânia ampliou os ataques de longo alcance contra alvos em território russo.

O governo Putin também enfrenta especulações sobre uma possível nova campanha de mobilização militar neste outono. O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, afirmou que o Kremlin pretende recrutar outros 300 mil soldados — uma estimativa atribuída ao governo ucraniano.

Eleição usada como termômetro pelo Kremlin

Essa eleição era tratada pelo Kremlin como particularmente importante, porque foi a primeira a ser realizada após o início da guerra da Ucrânia . O pleito serviria a Putin e sua equipe para medir o apoio do público russo ao conflito, que está em seu 5º ano sem perspectiva de ser finalizado.

Assim como o restante do aparato estatal russo, o Duma é subordinado ao governo Putin e as eleições parlamentares foram rigorosamente controladas e sem a participação de forças políticas contrárias à guerra na Ucrânia.

O Kremlin celebrou nesta segunda o resultado da eleição e afirmou que a vitória esmagadora do partido de Putin mostra que os russos apoiam o presidente .

“Esses indicadores apontam, é claro, para o mais alto nível de coesão da sociedade russa em torno do chefe de Estado”, declarou o porta-voz do Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, durante uma entrevista coletiva.

A Comissão Europeia afirmou que as eleições parlamentares russas mostraram uma “erosão contínua e crescente da democracia” e uma “repressão sistemática e institucionalizada” do governo Putin contra a oposição.

“As supostas eleições para a Duma representaram mais um grande retrocesso para a democracia russa. Seu resultado nunca esteve em dúvida. O Kremlin silenciou a dissidência, impediu a participação do único partido registrado que se opunha à sua guerra na Ucrânia e excluiu observadores eleitorais internacionais. O verniz de democracia é tudo o que resta na Rússia”, afirmou a alta representante da UE para a política externa, Kaja Kallas.

A oposição russa afirmou que a votação ficou longe de ser justa.

articles.title: Empresária fisga dourado de 18 kg pela primeira vez durante pescaria | G1
articles.standfirst: Mayara Teodoro da Silva estava com a família em uma pescaria no Rio Dourado, em Dourados (MS), quando fisgou, na primeira parada, o peixe de 1,05 metro e 18 quilos.
articles.summary: Mayara Teodoro da Silva estava com a família em uma pescaria no Rio Dourado, em Dourados (MS), quando fisgou, na primeira parada, o peixe de 1,05 metro e 18 quilos.
articles.body:
Mayara Teodoro da Silva, de 40 anos, fisgou pela primeira vez um dourado de aproximadamente 1,05 metro e 18 quilos durante uma pescaria em família, neste domingo (20), no Rio Dourados , no sul de Mato Grosso do Sul.

Ao g1 , Mayara contou que fisgou o peixe nos primeiros 30 minutos de pescaria, logo na primeira parada do grupo. Veja o vídeo acima.

Apesar de já ter participado de várias pescarias, Mayara contou que esta foi a primeira vez que fisgou um peixe tão grande. A captura foi marcada por emoção, nervosismo e até lágrimas.

“Foi muita emoção, um misto de alegria e nervosismo. Chorei muito. Fiquei nervosa e tremia”, contou.

Mayara Teodoro da Silva com o peixe dourado, figado em MS — Foto: Anna Júlia Azambuja

Após retirar o peixe da água, Mayara e a família decidiram encerrar a pescaria. “Quando peguei o peixe, paramos de pescar e fomos comemorar”, disse.

Para Mayara, o peixe de aproximadamente 1,05 metro representa uma conquista especial.

"Nós falamos que íamos atrás da barra de ouro, olha aqui ela", brincou.

Mayara ao lado do marido Laender Azambuja e o filho Eduardo Teodoro Azambuja — Foto: Anna Júlia Azambuja

Lei permite apenas a pesca “pesque e solte”

O dourado, conhecido como o "Rei do Rio" pelos pescadores, está com a captura proibida em Mato Grosso do Sul há seis anos. A restrição, que segue em vigor até 31 de março de 2027, busca preservar a espécie e prevê multas mais severas do que as aplicadas em outros casos de pesca irregular.

A lei permite apenas a pesca “pesque e solte” e a captura para consumo próprio por pescadores profissionais e ribeirinhos, além de exceções para pesquisa e criação autorizada. Um estudo técnico deverá avaliar a situação dos cardumes e definir se a proibição será mantida ou suspensa.

articles.title: Taubaté prorroga prazo de inscrição de startups em programa de incubação em Hub | G1
articles.standfirst: Inscrições para até 18 startups seguem abertas até 17 de outubro; programa oferece capacitações, mentorias e estrutura do HITT.
articles.summary: Inscrições para até 18 startups seguem abertas até 17 de outubro; programa oferece capacitações, mentorias e estrutura do HITT.
articles.body:
A Prefeitura de Taubaté prorrogou por mais 30 dias o prazo de inscrições do chamamento público para seleção de até 18 startups interessadas em participar do Programa de Incubação do HITT (Hub de Inovação Tecnológica de Taubaté). Com a prorrogação, as inscrições seguem abertas até 17 de outubro.

A iniciativa, coordenada pela Sedint (Secretaria de Desenvolvimento, Inovação, Agricultura e Turismo), busca fomentar o empreendedorismo inovador, estimular o desenvolvimento tecnológico, contribuir para a geração de emprego e renda e fortalecer o ecossistema de inovação de Taubaté. As startups participantes também terão o desafio de desenvolver soluções para problemas reais do município, em áreas como mobilidade, saúde, segurança e gestão pública.

O edital completo e as informações para inscrição estão disponíveis no site da Prefeitura de Taubaté

Por meio de parceria com o Sebrae (Serviço Brasileiro de Apoio às Micro e Pequenas Empresas) e a ABS (Associação Brasileira de Startups), as empresas selecionadas terão acesso gratuito a capacitações, mentorias e à infraestrutura disponível no HITT. O programa contempla negócios em diferentes estágios de desenvolvimento, com modalidades de pré-incubação, incubação e incubação avançada.

O programa foi estruturado para atender negócios em diferentes estágios de desenvolvimento. Os projetos poderão ingressar nas modalidades de pré-incubação, incubação ou incubação avançada, de acordo com o nível de maturidade da startup.

Na pré-incubação, destinada principalmente a projetos em fase de ideação ou validação, o trabalho será direcionado à estruturação do modelo de negócio, desenvolvimento do MVP (Produto Mínimo Viável) e validação inicial da solução. Essa etapa terá duração de até seis meses. A incubação será voltada às startups que já possuam um MVP desenvolvido ou estejam iniciando suas operações, com foco na validação de mercado, estruturação comercial e consolidação do produto ou serviço, pelo período de até 12 meses. inovação relevante, viabilidade técnica e potencial de impacto econômico.

Serão especialmente valorizadas propostas que apresentem conexão com setores estratégicos para a economia de Taubaté e da região, como os segmentos automotivo, metalmecânico, aeronáutico, industrial e logístico.

A seleção será realizada em etapas, incluindo análise documental, avaliação técnica do pré-projeto, apresentação da proposta em formato de pitch e classificação final.

Entre os critérios que serão considerados estão grau de inovação, potencial de mercado, escalabilidade, capacidade da equipe, viabilidade técnica e impacto econômico e social. A avaliação terá pontuação máxima de 100 pontos, sendo necessária pontuação mínima de 60 pontos para classificação.

articles.title: Redes de TV dos EUA suspendem cobertura conjunta da Casa Branca após Trump banir acesso de jornalistas | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente dos EUA baniu CNN, MS NOW e Politico de entrar na Casa Branca. Em retaliação, emissoras que fazem parte do 'pool' — entre elas a Fox News, aliada de Trump — anunciaram boicote em defesa dos jornalistas nesta segunda-feira (21).
articles.summary: Presidente dos EUA baniu CNN, MS NOW e Politico de entrar na Casa Branca. Em retaliação, emissoras que fazem parte do 'pool' — entre elas a Fox News, aliada de Trump — anunciaram boicote em defesa dos jornalistas nesta segunda-feira (21).
articles.body:
Cinco redes de TV dos Estados Unidos anunciaram nesta segunda-feira (21) que vão suspender a cobertura conjunta que fazem do governo dos EUA . A medida é uma retaliação à decisão do presidente norte-americano, Donald Trump, de banir o acesso à Casa Branca de alguns jornalistas , na semana passada.

➡️ Na sexta-feira (18), o presidente dos EUA anunciou que proibiria o acesso à Casa Branca de jornalistas das redes de TV CNN e MS NOW e do site Politico ( leia mais abaixo ).

As redes que participam do chamado "pool" de imprensa — uma cobertura conjunta de atos e pronunciamentos do governo Trump na Casa Branca — e que anunciaram a suspensão da cobertura são:

A Fox News é aliada do governo Trump . Em comunicado divulgado pela CNN Internacional e pelo jornal "The New York Times", o chefe da emissora em Washington, Bryan Boughton, respaldou o boicote . Mais tarde, a Fox News assinou um comunicado conjunto das cinco emissoras condenando a restrição:

"O público tem um interesse vital em receber informações precisas e independentes sobre o seu governo. Nenhuma administração deve restringir uma organização de notícias por discordar de suas reportagens", diz o comunicado.

👉 As cinco emissoras, que estão entre as maiores dos EUA , se revezam na captura de imagens de atos e pronunciamentos na Casa Branca. As imagens são distribuídas para as cinco redes e também para TVs locais dos EUA.

Como a CNN e a NBC (parte do grupo MS NOW) fazem parte do grupo de jornalistas proibidos por Trump de ingressar na Casa Branca, o "pool" ficou desfalcado . As cinco emissoras afirmaram que esse desfalque não será coberto, o que significa que, nesses dias, a cobertura será afetada.

Nesta segunda-feira, segundo a Fox News, o turno cabia à CNN, e, por isso, não houve imagens no "pool". Para os próximos dias, o desfalque pode também afetar a cobertura da agenda paralela à Assembleia Geral da ONU que Donald Trump fará na Casa Branca — como reuniões bilaterais com chefes de governos.

“Informamos que, a partir de hoje, o pool de emissoras de TV não fará a cobertura de eventos designados como cobertura em 'pool' do Presidente”, escreveu o chefe da Fox News em Washington, Bryan Boughton.

Repórter da CNN faz transmissão ao vivo em rua de Washington, nos Estados Unidos, após ser impedida de entrar na Casa Branca por determinação de Donald Trump, em 19 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Anna Rose Layden/ Reuters

Também nesta segunda, a CNN, a MS NOW e o Político entraram com um processo contra o governo Trump na Justiça norte-americana exigindo que a proibição seja derrubada e os crachás dos jornalistas sejam devolvidos.

No sábado (19), repórteres da CNN e da MS NOW foram proibidas de acessar a Casa Branca, e funcionários do governo Trump apreenderam os crachás das jornalistas.

👉 Ao longo do fim de semana, veículos de comunicação criticaram, em editoriais, a decisão de Trump, acusando o presidente dos EUA de cercear a liberdade de imprensa , prevista na Constituição dos Estados Unidos.

Nesta segunda, Trump negou que mire a liberdade de imprensa e afirmou que sua intenção foi combater as "fake news" , que, segundo ele, são espalhadas pelos veículos de imprensa banidos da Casa Branca. O presidente, no entanto, não apresentou provas de notícias falsas.

"A Casa Branca não está promovendo um ataque à imprensa livre, algo que eu valorizo. Ela está promovendo um ataque às FAKE NEWS, algo que cresceu como um câncer em nossos amados Estados Unidos da América. Elas são corruptas, intencionais, disseminadas, totalmente coordenadas e completamente fora de controle. São uma ameaça à nossa segurança nacional e precisam ser detidas, AGORA!", afirmou Trump, em sua rede social Truth Social.

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fala com repórteres antes de embarcar no Air Force One na Base Aérea Conjunta Andrews, em Maryland, em 9 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Foto de BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/AFP

Na sexta-feira (18), Donald Trump anunciou, por meio de uma publicação em sua rede social Truth Social, que baniria três veículos de comunicação de acessar a Casa Branca:

A CNN é uma das principais redes de televisão dos Estados Unidos.👉

A MS NOW é um canal de notícias por assinatura de viés liberal.

O Politico é um site especializado na cobertura política do país.

👉 Tradicionalmente, jornalistas de diferentes veículos dos EUA e do mundo têm acesso regular aos setores de imprensa da Casa Branca, para acompanhar entrevistas coletivas, pronunciamentos e anúncios no Salão Oval.

Como justificativa, Trump alegou, sem oferecer provas, que os veículos de imprensa banidos divulgavam notícias falsas. Os veículos negaram.

Os três veículos de comunicação banidos por Trump costumam fazer uma cobertura mais crítica ao governo dos EUA, mesmo assim eles são conhecidos como tendo um jornalismo consolidado. Os jornais afirmaram que entrarão nesta segunda com um processo na Justiça contra o banimento do governo Trump.

👉 Esta não é a primeira vez que Trump tenta dificultar o acesso de jornalistas à cobertura presidencial. No ano passado, seu governo restringiu o acesso da agência de notícias Associated Press (AP).

Além disso, a Casa Branca tem aberto mais espaço para veículos de imprensa e canais de redes sociais ideologicamente alinhados ao republicano.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Vincent Van Gogh: "I would rather die of passion than of boredom" The legendary artist's advice on not just blindly following daily routine, but knowing what we do
articles.summary: Vincent van Gogh was a Dutch painter, born in the Netherlands. It is surprising to know that though he's now seen as one of the most important artists.
articles.body: Vincent van Gogh was a Dutch painter, born in the Netherlands. It is surprising to know that though he's now seen as one of the most important artists in history, he remained mostly unrecognised during his lifetime and sold only a handful of paintings before he died.He took painting seriously only in his late twenties, after numerous failed attempts to be an art dealer, a teacher, and a preacher. Over roughly a decade, he produced nearly 900 paintings and more than 1,100 works on paper, including some of his most famous ones like "The Starry Night" and "Sunflowers."Some lines stay with us even long time after we read them, and keep reappearing in unexpected places, but by then we have already forgotten their original and actual meaning.That's basically what happened here. It sounds like the kind of thing a tortured artist would speak out in a raw, unguarded moment for years; that's exactly how it's been sold to us.But let us dig in to find out what Van Gogh really means to say.Quote of the dayI would rather die of passion than of boredom.Vincent Van GoghWhat does the quote meanIn October 1884, Van Gogh wrote a letter to his brother Theo in which he wrote these words, admiring the idea that it means to convey. Van Gogh says that he would rather live a life intensely, even if it costs you something, which is better than a life spent going through the motions.Boredom here does not just mean "having nothing to do." It's a kind of slow erosion, like just being there, doing the expected thing, feeling nothing, day after day. Passion, on the other hand, is risky. It can wear you out in unexpected ways, disappoint you, even end badly. But at least it means you were awake for your own life and doing what you know you are.How is this idea relevant today?This idea fits Van Gogh's actual life quite well. He gave up financial security, comfort, and conventional success to paint obsessively, often in poverty, often misunderstood, right up until his death.Similarly, even today, boredom hasn't gone anywhere; it's just changed its form. A lot of modern life is built around comfort and everyday patterns, like the same commute, the same feed, the same routines that ask very little of us emotionally. Scrolling has replaced staring out the window, but the numbness is similar. At the same time, there's real pressure to keep things safe, like the "sensible" job, the "practical" choice, the path with the least risk of failure.But the artist encourages us to take some risks and make life interesting, not being reckless but just knowing what you do because it's genuinely right for you.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: 10 lions found dead in suspected poisoning at wildlife reserve
articles.summary: An investigation is underway to establish the definitive cause of the deaths inside the area where wildlife including lions, elephants and black rhinos live.
articles.body:
Ten lions have been found dead in a suspected poisoning incident at Tanzania's UNESCO-listed Ngorongoro Conservation Area, according to the authorities.

"The Ngorongoro Conservation Area Authority (NCAA) regrets to inform the public that ten (10) lions were found dead on September 18, 2026 in the Ndutu area," the wildlife reserve said in a statement .

Authorities said preliminary findings suggest that the lions died after "ingesting poison," adding that an expert investigation was ongoing "to determine the cause of the incident and identify those responsible."

Ngorongoro has been the scene of long-standing tensions between the authorities and the local nomadic community. Clashes have sometimes turned deadly since the government launched an eviction program in 2022.

The Tanzanian government argues that population growth is encroaching on wildlife habitat, with the number of people living in Ngorongoro rising from about 8,000 in 1959 to more than 100,000.

According to UNESCO , Ngorongoro Conservation Area is home to a population of about 25,000 large animals, including the densest known population of lions.

The International Union for Conservation of Nature classifies lions as vulnerable and says their numbers are declining. Threats facing the species include habitat loss, declining prey populations and human-wildlife conflict.

Since June, at least 20 elephants have died in Kenya's Amboseli ecosystem, near the Tanzanian border, from suspected pesticide poisoning, although authorities could not establish whether the deaths were accidental or deliberate.

Kenya has previously recorded incidents of elephants being poisoned as a result of poaching and human-wildlife conflict. But officials say it's the first time in decades the region has recorded elephant deaths on this scale, according to CBS News' partner network BBC News .

articles.title: IIT Bombay student suicide: Faculty march in support of prof Doolla; victim's father claims casteism - top developments
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: IIT-Bombay's faculty forum on Monday came out in support of prof Suryanarayana Doolla, after the institute removed him as dean (administrat.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: IIT-Bombay's faculty forum on Monday came out in support of prof Suryanarayana Doolla, after the institute removed him as dean (administrative affairs) amid protests over the death of 22-year-old student Sahil Wakode.Also check: IIT Bombay Student Suicide Live Updates: Forensic team reaches campus; students await open house with directorThe faculty forum said Doolla had been temporarily relieved of his administrative duties to facilitate an independent and unbiased investigation into Wakode's death, and clarified that he continues to be a faculty member at the institute.Faculty forum marches in supportIn a statement, faculty forum president prof Rajkumar S Pant said, "We would like to clarify that contrary to several media reports, Prof Suryanarayana Doolla has not been suspended from his service from IIT Bombay and continues to be a member of the institute's faculty in good standing."The forum said Doolla, during his tenure as dean (student affairs), had been instrumental in setting up several initiatives for the welfare of students on campus."The Faculty Forum of IIT Bombay stands strongly with our colleague Prof Suryanarayana Doolla," the statement said, while expressing concern over what it called "false and misleading media reports" about him.The forum also announced a campus march from the Nandan Nilekani Main Building on Monday to express solidarity with Doolla.Doolla named in FIRIIT-Bombay removed Doolla from the post of dean (administrative affairs) with immediate effect amid protests following Wakode's death. Doolla has been named in an FIR filed on the basis of the student's family's complaint.Police have registered a case under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The Crime Branch is investigating the case.Wakode, a second-year BTech student in the Department of Energy Science and Engineering, was found hanging from the ceiling fan in his hostel room on the institute's Powai campus on September 18.Congress protests, student's father alleges 'casteism'The student's death has triggered protests on the IIT-Bombay campus, with students raising allegations of academic pressure, caste discrimination and institutional harassment.Police on Monday detained Youth Congress workers who were protesting outside the IIT-Bombay gate. Security in and around the campus was also increased following the protests.Wakode's father, Ravindra Wakode, has alleged that his son had faced caste-based mocking and harassment from a professor and the institute administration. He claimed that his son had spoken about being repeatedly mocked and targeted on caste lines.The family has demanded a probe into the circumstances surrounding Wakode's death.IIT-Bombay apologises over earlier statementThe institute issued a public apology after students accused it of "defaming" Wakode without a detailed inquiry."In view of the ongoing investigation, it was inappropriate to have set out or characterised details relating to the events preceding Sahil's demise before they had been duly established through the appropriate investigative process," IIT-Bombay said.In an earlier statement, the institute had said Wakode was allegedly caught using a mobile phone during a mid-semester examination and had uploaded the examination question paper to ChatGPT to seek answers. It had said no disciplinary action had been initiated against him.Open House awaitedAmid the protests, IIT-Bombay announced to hold an Open House with students on Monday at the Convocation Hall. Students have been asked to submit their questions through a designated form, with the queries to be taken up during the moderated session.The interaction is expected to give students an opportunity to raise their concerns and demands directly with the institute authorities.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Only 2 people called me in 3 years’: Indian woman shares ‘reality of NRI’ after moving to US
articles.summary: US News: An Indian woman living in Chicago has opened up about her experience of staying in touch with people in India, saying she received calls from only two.
articles.body: An Indian woman living in Chicago has opened up about her experience of staying in touch with people in India, saying she received calls from only two people during her three years in the US, apart from her immediate family. Her remarks came as she questioned why Indians who move abroad are often accused of becoming “detached” from those back home.Kanishka Jasoria shared her thoughts in an Instagram video, where she spoke about how communication and relationships can change after relocating overseas.‘I’ve received calls from only two people’“Whenever people move abroad, why does everyone living back in India say, ‘You’ve become detached’?” Jasoria said in the video.She then described the two calls she received. According to her, the first person asked how she was managing life without her family and how she had handled practical matters such as getting a loan.The second person, she said, questioned why she had moved abroad without informing them.“And you ask, ‘Why do you feel detached?’ There isn't even a need to ask for a reason, bro,” Jasoria said.The video carried the text “Reality of NRI”, while Jasoria captioned the post, “Based on true events”.‘Relationships need effort from both sides’Jasoria's comments focused on how moving to another country can affect personal relationships, particularly when communication is not reciprocated. Her experience also questioned the expectation that people living abroad should always be the ones making an effort to stay in touch with those back home.The video drew reactions from social media users, with several saying they could relate to her experience.“Sad but true,” one user commented.Another user shared their own experience after moving to Italy, saying that people in India had earlier warned they would forget them after moving abroad. However, after relocating, the person said they sometimes felt lonely and found it difficult to get responses when they called or messaged people back home.Another user wrote, “Sometimes distance reveals who really cares,” while another said, “Relationships need effort from both sides.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Louisiana neighbours fought over a 70-foot strip of land; after signs, bright lights and even a dead cow appeared near the boundary, an appeals court upheld $15,000 in damages and an injunction
articles.summary: US News: A property boundary dispute between two neighbouring families in Louisiana went from arguments over a 70-foot strip of land to large “No trespassing” .
articles.body: A property boundary dispute between two neighbouring families in Louisiana went from arguments over a 70-foot strip of land to large “No trespassing” signs, bright lights, loud generators and a dead cow placed near the disputed boundary. The Louisiana Court of Appeal, Second Circuit, has now upheld a lower court ruling that fixed the boundary at an old downed fence and ordered one family to pay $15,000 in damages.Jesse Justin Colvin and Ruby Sue Hill Colvin bought a 23-acre property in Union Parish in 2012 and made it their home. Robert Bradford Jones and Roni Michelle Reppond Jones bought a one-acre property nearby in 2014 and also lived there. According to Find Law, the court record says the families were friends and good neighbours for more than a decade before the property line became disputed.The disagreement centred on a strip of timber and undergrowth about 70 feet deep between the properties. The Colvins argued that the strip was entirely within their property and pointed to 1989 and 2012 surveys. The Joneses, however, said the boundary was an old combination or wire fence located further south. The fence was down, but remnants of it remained.As the disagreement continued, the Colvins put “No trespassing” signs along the surveyed property line. When the Joneses continued to claim the disputed area, the Colvins put up larger signs. The dispute eventually reached court in September 2023, when the Colvins filed a lawsuit seeking to have the boundary formally fixed.Court fixes boundaryThe case involved several surveys and testimony about the old fence. A 2012 survey by professional land surveyor James Michael Duty showed the “old wire fence (down)” south of the northern boundary of the Colvin property. Duty testified that the fence shown in his survey was in the same location as the downed combination fence identified in an earlier survey.Duty said the recorded property line was north of the old fence and that the 2012 survey matched the public records. Jesse Colvin also acknowledged that the 2012 survey referred to the old fence line.However, Jesse testified that he had the property surveyed again in 2022 because he did not know where the property line was. He said steel posts placed by his grandchildren were positioned according to that survey. He also acknowledged that before the dispute, he had never visited the northern boundary in question and had never kept livestock or cut trees there.The Joneses gave a different account of their use of the area. Robert Jones said he believed the old fence marked the boundary when he bought the property and that he had used the disputed area for hunting. He admitted that he had not conducted a survey and did not know the exact property lines on the eastern and western sides of his property.The trial court considered the surveys, witness testimony and evidence before deciding that the title records could not settle the disputed boundary. It found that the old downed fence represented the limits established by possession and fixed the boundary there.The Colvins challenged that decision before the appeals court. They argued that the boundary should instead be decided according to their title and the surveys. The appeals court rejected the argument and said the trial court had not made a clear error in fixing the boundary at the old fence.Signs, lights and dead cowThe boundary argument was not the only issue before the court. The Joneses also sought damages and a permanent injunction, saying the Colvins interfered with their use of their property.According to the court record, Jesse Colvin installed orange construction fencing near the boundary and, on April 11, 2023, put a series of 8-by-12-foot commercial signs along the Joneses’ property line. The signs said “Private property, no trespass”.On May 4, 2023, Jesse moved one of his dead cows into the wooded area near the Joneses. He said he had placed it there temporarily until he found a place to bury it. But the court noted that he did not deny telling Robert Jones during a recorded call, “I was fucking with you with the dead cow.”Later, on May 20, Jesse erected three larger signs, each measuring four feet by 16 feet and mounted on eight-foot poles. They were placed about 10 feet from the northern boundary and faced the Jones property.Two fluorescent orange signs carried the words “No trespassing from neighbours” along with poop-emoji symbols. The third said “J-one hog farm coming soon”. Jesse said the signs were prompted by a letter from Robert Jones. The trial court, however, found that the letter had simply asked the families to end their dispute.Three days later, on May 23, Jesse installed lights to illuminate the signs. The lights were powered by a generator. Robert Jones testified that the generator was loud enough to make his whole house vibrate. Jesse admitted that he illuminated the signs specifically to send Robert a message to leave him alone.Court upholds injunction and $15,000 damagesThe Joneses argued that the signs, dead cow, fencing, bright lights and generator noise substantially interfered with their enjoyment of their home. The trial court agreed and found that Jesse's actions were intentional, served no legitimate purpose and caused the Joneses fear, anxiety and loss of enjoyment of their backyard.The court ordered the Colvins to remove the signs, posts, lights and other flagging materials and prohibited similar materials from being placed at the disputed location.The Colvins argued on appeal that the Joneses had suffered only inconvenience and had not shown physical property damage, medical evidence of distress or financial loss. The appeals court did not accept that argument.The court referred to Louisiana law, under which a landowner cannot carry out work on their property that deprives a neighbour of the ability to enjoy their own property or causes damage. It also noted that an injunction can be granted when there is substantial interference with the peaceful use of property and the problem is likely to continue without court intervention.The appeals court said the evidence supported the lower court's finding that the conduct created real damage and irreparable injury. It also upheld the damages awarded to Robert and Roni Jones.The lower court had ordered Jesse Colvin to pay $7,500 to each of the Joneses, bringing the total damages to $15,000.The Louisiana Court of Appeal, Second Circuit, decided the case on January 14, 2026. It affirmed the lower court's ruling in full, including the boundary fixed at the old downed fence, the permanent injunction and the $15,000 damages award. The Colvins were also ordered to pay the costs of the appeal.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Cate Blanchett latest star to ask theatre audience to stop filming
articles.summary: The A-list actress is the latest star to ask fans to put their phones away during performances.
articles.body:
A-list actress Cate Blanchett has become the latest star to make a plea for theatre audiences to put their phones away during performances.

The Australian film and stage actor and producer was appearing at London's National Theatre in Electra/Persona.

During the curtain call on Friday, Blanchett said: "There are few places on this planet where we can simply be together and be present.

"I understand you like filming the curtain call – and it is kind of flattering in a way – but for anyone who is filming the show, please don't, because it spoils it for the next group of people who come in and are present with us. So thank you very much."

The two-time Oscar winner's words were greeted with cheers and clapping from the audience.

One audience member explained what had happened earlier in the performance, saying that the filming took place between two acts: "I was there on Friday, so just to clarify what happened: after the first act, while they were changing and preparing for the second, latecomers were being let in, the staff were cleaning the stage, and the cast were doing their makeup on stage.

"Cate noticed someone recording during that break. She came towards the front of the stage and gestured "no, no, no" with her finger for them to stop. She also mentioned it to the audience at the very end before they left," the theatre-goer wrote on Instagram .

"The person wasn't filming the actual performance, but the interval between the two acts while the cast were still on stage. To be fair, people do this quite often and the staff usually don't say anything. It was my third time seeing the play, and I've seen people film during that break every time. Friday was simply the first time I saw Cate notice it herself, just after she had finished doing her makeup."

Electra/Persona is a new play written and directed by Benedict Andrews that combines the Sophocles tragedy Electra with Ingmar Bergman's film Persona.

The play, which is on until 10 October, sees Blanchett sharing the roles of Electra/Elisabeth and Clytemnestra/Alma with her co-star Nina Hoss, determined by a coin toss live on stage every night ahead of each performance.

Rosamund Pike calls out audience member for texting during show

Loud eaters and phones nearly spoiled my cinema trip - and it's not just me

Many theatres, like cinemas, ask audiences to switch off their mobile phones during performances.

Rosamund Pike called out an audience member for texting during an emotional moment from her performance in West End play Inter Alia earlier this year, saying: "When I feel that and see it, it's hard."

Cynthia Erivo interrupted her recent performance of Dracula after spotting an audience member filming. And Andrew Scott halted his "to be or not to be" soliloquy in Hamlet, a few years back, after someone started using a laptop.

Other stars including Daniel Craig, Hugh Jackman and Patti LuPone have all made similar criticisms, while Lesley Manville told BBC Radio 4 earlier this year that she found it "insulting" when punters took photos, even of curtain calls.

articles.title: Divorce is ‘illegal’ in these two countries? What happens when marriages break down there
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Divorce is a legal option in most parts of the world, allowing a married couple to formally end a marriage. But the Philippines and Vatican City are t.
articles.body: Divorce is a legal option in most parts of the world, allowing a married couple to formally end a marriage. But the Philippines and Vatican City are two places often cited as exceptions. The Philippines has no general divorce law for most marriages, while its Muslim Personal Law provides specific forms of divorce. In the Vatican's Catholic canon-law framework, a valid and consummated sacramental marriage cannot be dissolved by human authority except by death, although canon law provides for separation, declarations of nullity and certain other forms of dissolution in specific circumstances. Here is what the official legal sources say.Philippines: No general divorce lawThe Philippines does not have a general divorce law for most married couples. Instead, Philippine family law provides legal routes such as legal separation, annulment and declaration of nullity of marriage. Legal separation, however, does not end the marriage itself. A couple may be allowed to live separately, but the marriage bond remains. This distinction is important because legal separation is not the same as divorce. A person who is legally separated is still married and cannot simply marry someone else as a divorced person could.According to the Family Code of the Philippines, legal separation and the declaration of nullity or annulment of marriage are provided for under Philippine family law.What happens when a marriage breaks down?Philippine law provides grounds for legal separation. These include circumstances such as repeated physical violence, sexual infidelity, abandonment and certain criminal convictions. But even when a court grants legal separation, the marriage itself is not dissolved. Couples can also go to court seeking an annulment or a declaration of absolute nullity, depending on the legal circumstances of the marriage.These proceedings are different from divorce because they deal with the validity of the marriage rather than simply ending a valid marriage because the relationship has broken down. The Philippine legal system therefore gives couples certain ways to end their marital obligations or establish that a marriage was legally invalid, but it does not provide the ordinary divorce process available in many other countries.There is also an important qualification in cases involving a Filipino spouse and a foreign spouse. According to Article 26(2) of the Family Code, certain divorces validly obtained abroad can have legal effects in the Philippines, including allowing the Filipino spouse to acquire the capacity to remarry, subject to recognition under Philippine law.There is an important exception for Muslim FilipinosThe description of the Philippines as a country where “divorce is illegal” has an important qualification. The country has a separate Code of Muslim Personal Laws. According to the Supreme Court E-Library, this code applies to certain Muslim marriages and specifically contains provisions dealing with marriage and divorce. Article 45 of the code defines divorce as the formal dissolution of the marriage bond and lists several forms, including talaq, khul' and judicial divorce or faskh.The code also states that it applies to marriages where both parties are Muslims, or in specified circumstances where only the husband is Muslim and the marriage was solemnised according to Muslim law or the code.Vatican City: Marriage is considered indissolubleThe situation in Vatican City is different. The Catholic Church's Code of Canon Law states that the essential properties of Christian marriage are unity and indissolubility. It also says that a valid and consummated sacramental marriage cannot be dissolved by any human power or for any reason other than death, according to the Code of Canon Law. That is the central reason Vatican City is included in lists of places without divorce.A valid sacramental marriage is not treated as a marriage that can simply be terminated through a divorce proceeding under Catholic canon law. However, canon law provides for specific circumstances in which certain marriages can be dissolved. According to Canon 1142 of the Code of Canon Law, a non-consummated marriage can, for a just cause, be dissolved by the Roman Pontiff.This does not mean that every marriage involving Catholics is automatically considered valid and permanent regardless of circumstances. The Catholic Church has a formal process through which a marriage can be declared null. An annulment, in this context, is not the Catholic equivalent of a divorce. A declaration of nullity concerns whether a valid marriage existed according to the requirements of canon law. The Vatican's Code of Canon Law contains specific procedures for cases concerning the declaration of nullity of marriage.Can married couples live separately?Yes. The Vatican's canon law also contains provisions concerning the separation of spouses. According to the Code of Canon Law, spouses can have a legitimate reason to separate while maintaining the distinction between separation and dissolution of the marriage. So the absence of divorce does not mean that couples must necessarily continue living together in every circumstance. The key difference is that separation does not dissolve a valid marriage.So is divorce actually 'illegal' in both countries?In the Philippines, there is no general divorce law applicable to most marriages, but divorce is expressly provided for under the country's Muslim Personal Law in cases covered by that code. Certain divorces obtained abroad can also have legal effects under Philippine law. In Vatican City, Catholic canon law does not provide for the divorce of a valid and consummated sacramental marriage. It does, however, provide procedures for separation and declarations of nullity, as well as limited forms of dissolution in specific circumstances.That makes the legal reality more nuanced than the commonly repeated two-country claim and also explains why the Philippines and Vatican City continue to appear on lists of places without a general divorce system.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Napa family rebuilt its winery after the 2017 wildfire for over $30 million; nine years later, debt has reached $37 million and the 50-year-old estate faces foreclosure
articles.summary: US News: The last winery foreclosure in California happened in 1992, but it may happen again soon. Ray Signorello's father founded their winery when he was jus.
articles.body: The last winery foreclosure in California happened in 1992, but it may happen again soon. Ray Signorello's father founded their winery when he was just 14 years old. Next year, it is all set to celebrate its golden jubilee, but it might not be able to.On October 2nd, Napa's Signorello Estate is set to be unceremoniously auctioned off in a small, concrete courtyard next to the Napa County Courthouse. Ray Signorello suspects that the winning bidder might be the lender, whom he owes $37 million- American AgCredit, a borrower-owned cooperative that finances agriculture businesses.A series of bad fortunesIn the 2017 Atlas Fire, Signorello's winery, set on a hilltop off Napa's Silverado Trail was the first to have burned to the ground. The winery, hospitality space and Signorello's home were destroyed completely. But there were two silver linings: his 38-year-old Chardonnay vines, which he believes are the second-oldest in Napa Valley, and his 28-year-old Cabernet vines, had survived.Rebuilding it took seven years and a series of delays in permitting, the pandemic, tariffs and the wine crisis. The permitting process with Napa County “dragged on,” and he wasn’t allowed to start construction until 2020. Then the pandemic hit, significantly impacting his restaurant wine business, which at the time, accounted for more than 50% of his sales. Construction on the winery also stalled, while his costs, especially for concrete and steel, "went through the roof." “Every day, I’d get a call about how it’s going to take longer and cost more,” Signorello said to the San Francisco Chronicle, and he repeatedly had to go back to American AgCredit to increase the loan.At the same time, he had to engage in a long legal battle with his insurance company, which he said originally offered to pay him just $300 a foot for his losses. “You can’t build a shack for $300 (a foot),” he said. It cost him $1 million in legal fees to fight the company, and he “still only got 75% of what I should have.”Finally in June 2024, Signorello opened the doors to its new winery. It featured state-of-the-art, automated equipment and doors Signorello can open from his cell phone. It cost “north of $30 million,” he said, double his original estimate. But in the seven years it took to rebuild his business, the wine world had changed a lot. When Signorello obtained his original loan for about $10 million in 2018, wine sales were in a period of steady growth. They exploded in 2020, largely due to pandemic pantry loading. During those good years, while many of his neighbours were enjoying success, Signorello said his brand “went downhill” as he was relegated to hosting visitors in a modest trailer and his wine club numbers “slowly faded off.” Starting in 2023, global wine sales began to drop, and have continued their downward trend in the years since.Canada's US alcohol ban in retaliation for Trump's tariffs cost a 20% blow to his sales and the custom crush market he had bet on evaporated too. Smoke from another round of Napa Valley wildfires destroyed his entire 2020 red grape crop, meaning that in a few years, he’d have no red wine, the bulk of his production, to sell from that vintage.“I've done this for 38 years. It's my livelihood, it's my family's livelihood,” Signorello said. “Maybe you could get through one or two of those, but when you put them all together — I'm not a magician,” he added. “I don't think there's anybody else that could have done much different.”A looming foreclosureSince 2018, Signorello said the interest rate on his loan from American AgCredit has skyrocketed, from 4.75% to 12.6% in 2024, due to him being “out of compliance.” He admitted that he missed payments and said American Ag Credit, the county’s fifth-largest farm credit association, started pressuring him to repay it. “They probably didn't like the loan,” he said. “They realised — bad market, big loan — this is a problem for us.”Since Signorello did not have $37 million, he hired Canada-based BMO Capital Markets, a mergers and acquisitions leader in US wine to help him find an investor or buyer. But after a year of searching, “they got nothing,” he said. “I couldn’t solve the problem.”After the notice of sale posted in July, Signorello said longtime customers of his winery offered American AgCredit $16 million, all cash, but the creditor turned it down. The night before the Aug. 28 auction was scheduled to take place, Signorello made one last effort to save the winery and filed for bankruptcy, which delayed the auction a month and would, he hoped, force a sale through a more traditional courthouse auction.The filing included a stalking horse offer from his customers, worth $20 million. The filing also included a debtor-in-possession (DIP) financing agreement, which would allow Signorello to continue operating through the bankruptcy process. It would also mean that Amar Doman and Ashley Cooper, who financed the filing, would get paid back before American AgCredit in the case of a sale.American AgCredit opposed the DIP financing agreement in court, and Signorello said he felt he had no choice but to withdraw the bankruptcy filing. The auction is back on, now scheduled for October 2. “This process is a joke. It's a courtroom step auction with cash, so (bidders) literally have to bring like 30 or 40 checks with them,” Signorello said. “Usually these things are quite small. They're $100,000 deals. Wineries of this nature are not sold on corporate steps in front of a fountain.”Even in the wake of the wine crisis, which has led to a surge in closures and sales, winery foreclosures remain incredibly rare in California; wineries are more often auctioned off through distress sales via the bankruptcy process. In a foreclosure, which is typically initiated by a lender or creditor, a winery’s land, buildings, equipment and intellectual property are seized as collateral. In a bankruptcy, usually initiated by the winery, the court supervises a sale or liquidation.Signorello said that he finds American AgCredit’s strategy perplexing. The quiet real estate market for California wine isn’t showing signs of rebounding any time soon, and it could be a while before the institution gets a better offer than the $20 million it rejected. In the meantime, American AgCredit will either have to tend the vines and operate the winery — which will likely require obtaining a new ABC license — or shut it down with the 2026 fermentations still underway. 10 employees (including a vineyard foreman who's worked there since 1989) will lose their jobs and the organic vineyards and 50-year family legacy could be shut down.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Archaeologists uncover Celtic sacred site near Cirencester with over 150 coins, broken miniature shields and spears buried as offerings
articles.summary: UK News: Archaeologists working near Cirencester in the Cotswolds have uncovered a Celtic sacred site dating to the late Iron Age, containing coins, spearheads.
articles.body: Archaeologists working near Cirencester in the Cotswolds have uncovered a Celtic sacred site dating to the late Iron Age, containing coins, spearheads, miniature shields linked to ritual activity before the Roman invasion. A metal detectorist first found the site in 2020. A Royal Agricultural University training excavation for MSc students has now revealed its scale.Researchers later relocated the original hoard pit and found that it had been placed within a sacred area marked by a pavement. Nearby, spears had been pushed into the ground, while deliberately broken miniature shields appear to have been left as offerings to Celtic gods.What archaeologists found inside the Celtic sacred siteThe site lies near Cirencester in the Cotswolds and likely dates to the late Iron Age, roughly 100 BC to AD 43. Archaeologists found a cobbled area that marked a sacred space. The stones had been worn flat, suggesting that people repeatedly moved around the area during ceremonies. The excavation also located the pit where the original coin hoard had been buried. Several spears had been placed in the soil, often vertically.Others were miniature bronze spears, and some were less than an inch long. Together, these findings indicate a ritual space where people made offerings. The worn pavement suggests, according to Horton, some form of mass processional activity around the central area. The spears and the deliberately broken miniature weapons point to a place where offerings were made.What do the miniature shields reveal about the ancient siteArchaeologists found model swords and scabbards, daggers and shields made from bronze. Many of these objects had been deliberately broken. Researchers interpret them as votives, or offerings to the gods. Their broken condition indicates they were not meant to be used again. The excavation also uncovered iron spears and miniature bronze spears, some less than an inch long.The spears had been pushed into the soil, according to Horton, to 'protect' the central area. Beneath them there were small pits cut into the Cotswold limestone. The pits contained fine soil but no artefacts. They may have been made for planting trees or bushes, suggesting the presence of a sacred grove.Ancient coins reveal the site’s connection to the DobunniThe coins provide clues about the people who used the sacred site. Many carry a distinctive three-tailed horse motif linked to the Dobunni, a tribe that lived across Gloucestershire, North Somerset, southern Worcestershire and western Oxfordshire. According to Horton (The RAU's Pro Vice-Chancellor for Research and Director of its Cultural Heritage Institute), their capital was at Bagendon, just a few miles from the excavation.The hoard contained more than 150 silver and bronze coins and metalwork. Dobunni coinage was likely issued by tribal leaders between about 50 BC and AD 20. Some of the coins are linked to Bodvic, a Dobunni leader. Researchers believe the site was probably a natural place or grove where people made offerings to Celtic gods. Its location and finds connect it to the religious landscape of the Dobunni and the nearby tribal centre at Bagendon.Why the discovery matters for understanding Celtic religionThe excavation gives archaeologists direct evidence of religious activity at the end of the Iron Age, a period when archaeologists have limited evidence about Celtic beliefs. Written accounts by classical writers provide some information about Iron Age and Celtic religion, but the remains at this site offer physical clues about how people used the space. The remains show how people used the space.They created a sacred area, moved around it, placed spears in the ground, and left offerings such as miniature shields. Broken bronze objects and possible tree-planting pits provide further clues about the site's use. The excavation area has now been refilled to protect it, while the Royal Agricultural University hopes to return for another excavation next year. At the same time, the Corinium Museum is raising funds to conserve and display the objects.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Texas recycled 650,000 pounds of discarded oyster shells to rebuild 4.5 acres of reef in St. Charles Bay
articles.summary: US News: Discarded oyster shells are being given a second life along the Texas coast, where researchers used them to rebuild reefs. A final report describes ho.
articles.body: Discarded oyster shells are being given a second life along the Texas coast, where researchers used them to rebuild reefs. A final report describes how the ‘Sink Your Shucks’ programme collected more than 650,000 pounds of shells from restaurants and oyster farms during the period. Reclaimed shells, once quarantined, were used in restoration projects, including 4.5 acres of oyster reef built in St. Charles Bay in May 2022, which expanded an existing restoration area to 18 acres. According to Texas A&M University Corpus Christi, the project also involved local communities, with volunteers placing recycled shells into mesh bags. Monitoring found that oysters began settling on the newly built reefs soon after construction and grew rapidly during the two-year study.How recycled oyster shells helped rebuild 4.5 acres of Texas reefThe project addressed a key challenge in oyster reef restoration that shells are needed to rebuild reefs, but suitable material can be limited and costly. The ‘Sink Your Shucks’ programme helped solve this by collecting discarded shells from seafood businesses and redirecting them to restoration sites. During the project, the programme grew from two restaurant contributors to 10 restaurant partners and three oyster farms. Shells were collected one to three times a week and transported to a stockpile at the Port of Corpus Christi. They were then quarantined for at least six months before being used for restoration. By the end of the project, more than 650,000 pounds of oyster shells had been reclaimed, nearly three times the original target of 225,000 pounds.How recycled oyster shells helped build new reefs in St. Charles BayIn May 2022, the project used recycled oyster shells to build 4.5 acres of intertidal and subtidal reef in St. Charles Bay. This expanded an existing restoration area to 18 acres. Researchers then placed sampling trays at six sites to track oyster settlement and growth. During the first three months, oysters on the intertidal reefs grew at an average rate of 0.97 millimetres per day, compared with 0.95 millimetres per day on the subtidal reefs. The number of oysters increased over time at both reef types, although the subtidal sites recorded higher densities. Oysters began settling on the newly built reefs soon after construction. Six months later, the subtidal reefs had an average of 286 oysters per tray, while the intertidal reefs recorded an average of 51 oysters per tray after 12 months.Why oyster reefs matter for Texas coastal ecosystemsOyster reefs serve several important roles along the Texas coast. The report says they can help buffer storm surges, improve water quality, and provide habitat. They also support seafood, tourism, and recreation. St. Charles Bay is closed to commercial oyster harvesting, which allows restored oyster populations to develop without commercial harvesting pressure.The project also placed reefs near an eroding marsh shoreline beside Goose Island State Park. The marsh is home to the world’s only flock of migrating whooping cranes. By placing reef structures along vulnerable sections of the coast, the project aimed to help slow shoreline erosion while supporting oyster reef recovery. The restored areas also provide suitable conditions for oyster larvae to settle and grow naturally in the bay.How communities became part of the oyster reef restoration effortThe programme also involved local communities in the restoration work. In 2024, two events at Goose Island State Park brought together 250 people. Participants helped place 20 tons of recycled oyster shells into 3,000 cotton mesh bags. These bags were used to form new reefs along a vulnerable shoreline near the fishing pier. The programme also reached people who could not travel to Rockport through schools, festivals and local programmes. Educational activities explained how oysters filter water and provide habitat. The report says these activities helped increase awareness and stewardship of coastal resources. By combining shell collection, reef construction, monitoring and public participation, the programme linked discarded oyster shells with reef restoration along the Texas coast.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
